text:
Utah got the result it deserved, and the second period is where it earned it. Over those 20 minutes UTA generated 1.94 expected goals to New Jersey's 0.80, and the scoreboard caught up: MacKenzie Weegar's backhand made it 2-1, Nick Schmaltz scored on the power play at 12:05, and Lawson Crouse tipped in a 56 percent chance with 57 seconds left to make it 4-2. By the simulated-replay measure, UTA deserved to win 71 percent of the time, on 4.26 expected goals to NJD's 2.85.

The Devils kept pace in volume (66 shot attempts to 63) and answered twice through Luke Evangelista, a power-play tip-in in the first and an even-strength tip-in in the second, but few of their chances were good ones. Jesper Boqvist's backhand at 9:49 of the third cut it to 4-3 and made things tight for a few minutes. Jake Allen faced 31 shots and allowed five against 4.22 expected, a modest underperformance, while Karel Vejmelka stopped 30 of 33.

Vincent Trocheck settled it at 16:52 of the third with a wrist shot off feeds from Schmaltz and Clayton Keller. Mikhail Sergachev, the first star, picked up three assists, and Schmaltz added a goal and two helpers while his line outscored the Devils 2.83 to 0.59 in expected goals. Utah also won the special teams battle, scoring on two of four power plays against New Jersey's one in five.
